passage: Tuesday. It happened again today. I was answering in class and my voice cracked, right in the middle of "photosynthesis". It squeaked high and then dropped low. Two boys grinned. I felt my face heat up and almost stopped talking. But Parveen, who sits behind me, just whispered, "Keep going." So I did. I even laughed, and said, "Sorry, my voice has a mind of its own." A few people laughed with me and it stopped feeling so big. I'd rather laugh than go silent for weeks. Note to self: the crack isn't about how I feel, it's just my voice. Imran

qa.q: What word was Imran saying when Imran's voice cracked?
What was Imran feeling when Imran's voice cracked, and what changed?
qa.a: Imran was embarrassed and nearly stopped talking. Parveen's encouragement and Imran's own laugh made it feel smaller.

qa.q: What could Imran keep doing when Imran's voice cracks?
qa.a: Imran can laugh it off and keep going instead of going silent. It is physical, not emotional.

qa.q: How might Parveen have seen Imran's voice crack?
qa.a: Parveen treated it as nothing to fuss about and just whispered for Imran to keep going. Ignoring it was the kind thing.

grounding: A teenager's voice cracks in puberty and the teenager laughs it off instead of going silent.
